articleTitle: The Future for Variable Frequency Drive Predictive Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE IAS Pulp and Paper Industry Conference (PPIC)
abstract: Predictive maintenance continues to evolve using applied analytics to solve problems in manufacturing industries. Whether it's built into an end device, operating in the central control system, or deployed across an enterprise on various levels, analytics solutions can solve some of the toughest challenges. The scalability of an analytics solution can optimize the speed at which information is consolidated and presented to a user so they can optimize system performance. While these predictive maintenance features already exist in the drive, there is always a desire to know the status of this critical information at the right time by the right person to ensure the value of predictive maintenance is realized. Predictive models on top of artificial intelligence (AI) techniques will be the key to reliable drives operation in future. With a common framework for all components and consistent plantwide integration, systems will be designed with predictive models that can learn and adapt to actual drive usage patterns and predict remaining useful life (RUL) of the components. Goal today is the same as tomorrow - minimizing unplanned downtime and reducing unexpected losses.

articleTitle: Ride the Lightning (Protection) - All the Way to Ground
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE IAS Pulp and Paper Industry Conference (PPIC)
abstract: This paper breaks down lightning protection for industrial applications into its key elements, discussing the pros and cons along the way. What a lightning strike is, and what happens when lightning strikes a structure is defined. The paper also covers the whys and wherefores of how and when mitigation measures should be implemented. The discussion centers around: Strike quantification The published codes and guidelines Identifying/prioritizing assets for protection Strike modelling techniques Benefits of proper protection Importance of maintenance and upgrades. Protection of people and assets from lightning strikes in an industrial environment can be a complicated undertaking compared to typical residential or commercial applications. Mill sites are complex technological organisms and in addition to operational personnel, there are many expansive structures, systems, equipment, components, and combustible materials that are susceptible to damage caused directly or indirectly by lightning strikes. This paper delves into the principles of lightning protection, providing insight and guidance regarding the codes, standards, design considerations, and practicalities around assessment and implementation of effective mitigation in pulp and paper mills and other industrial environments.

articleTitle: A Better Approach Towards Verifying the Absence of Voltage Testing and Ensuring Workplace Safety
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE IAS Pulp and Paper Industry Conference (PPIC)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to underscore the importance of Absence of Voltage Testers (AVTs) in mitigating electrical hazards in worksite environments. Electrical incidents continue to pose a significant risk to personnel and property, demanding comprehensive safety measures. AVTs, as a frontline tool, play a pivotal role in ensuring the safety of personnel by accurately verifying the absence of voltage in electrical systems before maintenance or repair activities commence. Furthermore, the paper explores the AVT technology, addressing advancements that have enhanced their reliability and usability. The integration of AVTs into safety protocols is discussed, demonstrating how organizations can effectively incorporate these tools to promote a culture of safety and compliance with industry regulations.

articleTitle: Operations-Driven Safety and Reliability: Creating a Blue Ocean of Asset Reliability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE IAS Pulp and Paper Industry Conference (PPIC)
abstract: This Paper examines the competitive and saturated field of reliability engineering, traditionally dominated by quantitative methods like Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA), Reliability Centered Maintenance (RCM), and Root Cause Analysis (RCA). The traditional quantitative “red ocean” approach, where intense competition leaves little room for differentiation, is critiqued and contrasted to a shift towards a “blue ocean” of asset reliability based on Operations Driven Safety and Reliability (ODSR). The Blue Ocean argues for a paradigm shift that prioritizes human factors, operator involvement, and a culture of continuous improvement, transcending traditional methodologies. It introduces the ODSR approach, which emphasizes the integral role of operators in ensuring safety and reliability, advocating for a holistic view that sees operators not as sources of error but as invaluable assets capable of identifying and mitigating risks. The paper outlines a framework for operationazing this shift through the lens of Human Factors in Reliability, Operator Empowerment, Continuous Improvement, and Design for Safety and Reliability (DFSR). It contrasts “best practices” with “better practices,” suggesting that a dynamic approach to reliability management can foster a more engaged, proactive, and innovative organizational culture. Documented case studies validate the effectiveness of the ODSR approach. Conclusively, this article posits ODSR as a strategic pivot towards a more sustainable, competitive, and innovative future in reliability engineering. Organizations are encouraged to embrace this blue ocean of asset reliability, driving measurable improvements, including enhanced safety, efficiency, and overall performance.

articleTitle: Applications of NGRS in Multiple Source MV Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE IAS Pulp and Paper Industry Conference (PPIC)
abstract: Neutral grounding resistors (NGRs) are regularly used in medium voltage distribution systems for industrial facilities. When there is on-site generation and multiple sources of power, the complexity of applying NGRs can increase significantly. The industry standards and best practices have evolved over the years, and the sizing of each NGR cannot be completed in a vacuum. Having coordinated NGRs throughout a distribution system is critical for the protection of generators, transformers, and feeders during ground faults, especially since the separate NGRs will affect the fault current seen by the overall system. This paper is intended to provide suggestions and application notes to aid engineers when sizing NGRs for the overall MV power distribution system, including generators and transformers, to ensure all equipment is properly protected for the given system and application. The NGR sizing also considers minimizing equipment damage during ground faults and minimizing the total ground-fault current to reduce the likelihood of ground faults escalating into phase-to-phase arcing faults, thereby improving personnel safety. An applicable case study for a real paper mill is included to demonstrate the NGR sizing process, calculations, and considerations.

articleTitle: Real-Time Controller HIL Simulations for Motor Starting Studies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE IAS Pulp and Paper Industry Conference (PPIC)
abstract: In this paper a virtual plant is combined with the hardware controllers of a reduced voltage soft-starter and adjustable frequency motor drive to simulate motor starting interactions. During across the line motor starts, as well as reduced voltage starting, a sag condition typically occurs as the shaft comes up to full speed. In industrial power systems adjacent loads such as adjustable frequency motor drives may be impacted by this transient disturbance. The situation can be further aggravated when the common bus is fed from a back-up diesel-generator set. Using a real-time controller hardware-in-the-loop simulator this starting condition will be examined. The goal is to determine if the power flow remains in the safe operating area of the diesel-generator set and capture how the adjustable frequency drive's hardware controller reacts to the disturbance. Multiple starting scenarios are examined including reduced voltage primary reactor starting, reduced voltage solid-state soft-starter starting, and the number of parallel generators to determine how the adjustable frequency drive already operating a motor responds.

articleTitle: The Crucial Role of Cybersecurity in Operational Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE IAS Pulp and Paper Industry Conference (PPIC)
abstract: In an era where Internet Protocol (IP)-based networks and commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) hardware and software are prevalent in process industries, the threat of cyberattacks is on the rise. This paper underscores the criticality of this issue and advocates for a proactive approach to cybersecurity, where industry best practices are integrated into every new and existing system. Cybersecurity incidents present an increased risk to the business, manufacturing processes, and safety. As a result, companies have begun requiring that products and systems used on the production floor comply with industry Operational Technology (OT) cybersecurity codes and standards. However, individual devices and subsystems, modern and legacy, must unite in an allinclusive network ecosystem. Therefore, each company must develop cybersecurity strategies that align with industry best practices and standards as well as the company's risk tolerance level. This paper will focus on key cybersecurity strategies and take a comprehensive approach to implementation, including people, processes, and technology.

articleTitle: Medium Voltage Cable Systems at Aging Paper Mills: Life-Cycle Management of the Last Critical Asset
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE IAS Pulp and Paper Industry Conference (PPIC)
abstract: Over the past few decades, the electrical manufacturing industry has leveraged advances in both materials and manufacturing technologies to provide cables and cable accessories for medium voltage cable systems that are more cost effective and reliable. The reliability is designed in and tested as part of the manufacturing quality control process which is based on stringent IEEE and ICEA standards. However, once these components leave the factory, the reliability is left to the quality level of the handling, installation, and operation of these components. The industry has learned much in the last few decades about the physics behind cable reliability and longevity, and we no longer need to guess at the failure mechanism or the best practices for product selection, system design, installation techniques, commissioning tests, operations and maintenance or timing of asset replacement. Pulp and Paper mills have several critical areas in their operation including wood handling, chipping, pulping, pumping and conveyors, to name a few, which warrant continuous monitoring, cleaning, and are typically the focus of plant maintenance shutdowns. However, the medium voltage power distribution and electrification of these systems is undoubtedly a critical underlying asset to all areas of the plant. It is the purpose of this paper to provide best practices to assess and maintain the reliability of these medium voltage cable systems throughout their lifecycle.

articleTitle: Why Can't I Start My Motor? Demystifying Motor Relay Lockouts
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE IAS Pulp and Paper Industry Conference (PPIC)
abstract: As the driver of many vital processes, motors are by far the most proliferous heavy machinery found in industrial facilities. Protection & control is key to maximizing operational life and process availability. Motor protection relays often employ thermal modeling and start inhibits to estimate the motor's thermal state and block restart attempts to prevent overheating of the stator windings. Adequately and accurately setting a motor's thermal protection is both an art and science – one that can cause confusion for operators if not correctly executed. This paper reviews the fundamental concepts and configuration of motor thermal protection. Various factors that play into typical restart blocking logic will be discussed, accompanied by case studies illustrating the consequences of improper configuration. Methods of troubleshooting will be examined and suggestions for configuration with limited motor data will be provided to avoid inadvertent and unnecessary motor lockouts.

articleTitle: Solid-State Circuit Breaker Technologies – Advanced Protection and Control Capabilities for Forest Products Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE IAS Pulp and Paper Industry Conference (PPIC)
abstract: The emerging use of solid-state molded case circuit breakers, in industrial applications, marks a significant advancement in electrical control, safety, and digital power management. Compared to similar solid-state devices, new semiconductor technologies, along with various control developments and protection algorithms, metering capabilities and other enhancements, are making solid-state circuit breakers a valuable new digital control and protection tool for industrial users. As solid-state molded case circuit breakers continue to go through the typical evolutionary changes associated with any new technologies, the emergence of additional control and protection elements will be even more advantageous to industrial users. These include the SSC8's ability to be rapidly and remotely reset or re-enabled, the ability to collect load condition monitoring data, along with the reduction of dangerous arc flash incident energies. These new generation devices also provide abundant access to accurate and precise metering data along with more sophisticated load monitoring capabilities, including the ability to regulate or soft start connected loads. These innovative devices leverage the latest in semiconductor technologies to provide more precise and rapid control of electrical loads, enabling unprecedented levels of customization, automation, monitoring, safety, and protection within the digital power environments of progressive forest products businesses.

articleTitle: Control of AC Brushless Exciter to Regulate Power Factor on Large AFD Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE IAS Pulp and Paper Industry Conference (PPIC)
abstract: In high power low-speed, (pole count equal or greater than eight), motor applications using synchronous machines in place of induction type machines results in performance benefits. Induction motors draw magnetizing current from the source and the total reactive current diminishes the power factor and efficiency in high pole count applications. By substituting a salient pole synchronous motor the power factor can be controlled to near unity. A three phase AC-AC brushless exciter with a rotating rectifier is an option to supply the field excitation on the rotor. In this paper a high power adjustable frequency drive fed synchronous motor is presented as well as an AC PWM chopper as the source to the brushless exciter. The motor's field V-curve is shown along with the schematic of the system. The paper includes the performance of voltage and current of the main stator as well as the exciter regulation of power factor. The differences between brushed vs. brushless and DC vs. three phase AC excitation is described including AC motor drive starting.

articleTitle: Factory Acceptance Testing: From Three Different Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE IAS Pulp and Paper Industry Conference (PPIC)
abstract: For many projects in industry, a decision to specify acceptance testing in the factory of suppliers that manufacture equipment involves many tradeoffs. On the positive front, identifying defects and validating functional operation in the factory comes at a much lower up-front cost than discovering these in the field after equipment is installed. On the other end of the spectrum, the producer is burdened with up-front costs in developing suitable specifications for factory testing, causing possible delays in the project schedule, and impacting the time before equipment can be field commissioned and energized. This paper will focus on factory acceptance testing from the perspective of the product manufacturer, the project specifying engineer, and the producer/user, considering electrical equipment such as motors, switchgear, transformers, cables, as well as process control equipment like Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs), Distributed Control Systems (DCS), Human Machine Interfaces (HMIs) and remote I/O. What products should be considered for factory acceptance testing and those that should not be considered will be identified. Control of project schedule will be addressed, outlining when and for how long acceptance testing should occur during the project cycle. Finally, summary recommendations outlining when factory acceptance testing should be required for a proposed list of various types of electrical equipment will be reviewed, recommending which products should be factory tested prior to shipment.

articleTitle: Dismiss Your Fears: A Guide to Writing and Presenting a Paper at the IEEE Pulp and Paper Industry Conference
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE IAS Pulp and Paper Industry Conference (PPIC)
abstract: The IEEE is the world's largest technical professional organization, consisting of over 400,000 members, 39 Technical Societies and 7 Councils. The organization sponsors over 2,000 conferences per year. One of these conferences is the annual IEEE Pulp & Paper Industry Conference, sponsored by the Pulp & Paper Industry Committee (PPIC) of the Industry Applications Society (IAS). The objective of the Pulp and Paper Industry Committee is “To advance the theory and practice in the electrical field as related to the design and management of electrical systems within the pulp and paper industry.” To support this objective, the PPIC sponsors an annual technical conference, inviting engineers working for industry producers, consultants, and supplier companies across North America to participate in formal technical paper presentations, panel sessions and tutorials. This annual “reunion” of electrical peers in the industry typically includes between 125 and 150 registered participants. The 2023 IEEE IAS Pulp & Paper Industry Conference held June 11–16 in Spokane, Washington was a remarkable success. Several seasoned industry veterans, young engineering professionals and first-time attendees gathered to learn about the latest in process industry applications focused on uptime, reliability, and electrical safety. Sharing updates on industry standards, bettering best practices, and lessons learned from mill operations, perhaps left some of the registered attendees feeling compelled and inspired to share their professional experiences at a future PPIC Conference. Which of the registered pulp and paper industry professionals attending the annual Pulp and Paper Industry Conference are qualified to author and present a technical paper at a future event? The answer is every one of them! If the reader is an industry enthusiast who is inspired to do so, the purpose of this article is to offer a “how-to” guide to assist prospective authors to act on their inspiration. Details describing the step-by-step process to submit an abstract, compose a rough draft, respond to comments from peer reviewers, submit a final manuscript and present slides at a future conference are clearly defined. The author of this article encourages all to rise-up and commit to serve as an author at a future PPIC sponsored conference.

articleTitle: Capital Projects: The Good, Bad, and Ugly, Panel Moderator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE IAS Pulp and Paper Industry Conference (PPIC)
abstract: Successful execution of capital projects is an important part of many mill engineering roles. Staffing levels in mills today often dictate that project are executed by a combination of mill engineers, vendor engineers, and one (or more) outside consultant engineers.Further complicating the situation is that many of today's mills were built many years ago and employ electrical and automation systems from a variety of vendors and timeframes. This panel discussion will explore the good, bad and ugly of capital project execution and hopefully provide some insight to reduce the chance that your capital projects will keep you up at night . . . or end in depositions!
